values: Honesty; uphold and defend the truth at all times
Justice and fairness in dealing with others
Integrity; moral uprightness and sound character

themes.theme_description: Focus on growth, development, peer pressure and school environment.

topics.core_competency: The learner knows about growth and development in adolescents and the management of peer pressure.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: describe changes experienced during adolescence and their effects on the person (k, u).
use verbs (k, u).
identify challenges of peer pressures and how to manage them (k, u).
know the impacts of peer pressure on young people in decision-making. (k,u, v/a)
identify dangers of drug abuse, e.g. alcohol, marijuana, “weed”, cigarettes (k, u).
use appropriate vocabulary to overcome challenges associated with peer influence (k, u, s, gs).
explain what a diary is (k, u).
state why keeping a diary is important (k, u, v)
mention what to keep in a diary and how (k, u).

suggested_learning_activities.description: using prior knowledge, teacher guides learners to brainstorm on what adolescence is and the age at which it begins.
in groups, learners outline the biological changes experienced during adolescence.
learners discuss the effects of those changes on girls and boys in their groups.
teacher guides learners to identify specific terms related to adolescence and their equivalents in their local language.
learners translate a text on adolescence from English to their local language (quarter page).
teacher guides learners to understand a verb.
in their groups, learners list the verbs they know and use them to construct sentences.
the leaners identify and use key verbs that describe biological changes during adolescence.
the teacher probes learners to identify who peers are citing examples.
in their groups, leaners discuss challenges in managing relationships among young people.
leaners perform a dialogue on persuasion and resistance to peer pressure.
in groups, learners share the impact of peer pressure.
the teacher prompts learners to give their personal judgements on the impact of peer pressure.
learners read and respond to texts relating to peer influence.
learners write their personal experience on the effects of peer pressure.
the teacher guides leaners to brainstorm on what drug abuse is.
in their groups, the leaners name drugs that are abused locally and their effects.
the leaners answer questions from a dictated passage about drug abuse.
in groups, leaners write a short article for the local media explaining dangers of drug abuse.
the teacher groups leaners and provides them with passages/pictures relating to peer influence for them to interpret.
learners translate a passage about drug abuse from English into local language.
through a role-play, learners express their views clearly and coherently.
through question and answer, teacher guides leaners to brainstorm on what a diary is.
in their groups, learners study a sample diary provided by the teacher.
learners discuss the features/format of a diary.
in their groups, the leaners brainstorm on the type of information to keep in a diary.
the learners brainstorm on the advantages and disadvantages of keeping a diary.
the teacher probes leaners to identify how people in the past kept their information.
the teacher tasks learners to fill out a hypothetical diary for a week using appropriate tense.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: listens to a conversation and notes down perspectives on peer influence.
describes orally their experiences in managing peer pressure.
discusses the dangers of drug abuse.
writes a letter to a friend advising them against drug abuse giving reasons.
lists five verbs related to growth, maturation and relationships.
writes a persuasive dialogue on how one can resist peer pressure.
reads a passage on dangers of drug abuse and answers the questions accordingly.
translates a one-paragraph text on drug abuse or peer influence.
writes one-passage essay on the effects of drug abuse.
writes an expository essay on the advantages and disadvantage of keeping a diary.
debates on why diary is not popular.
designs a diary for a particular period such as a school term, etc.
writes an argumentative composition comparing traditional ways to the modern ways of storing information.

suggested_uses: use electronic devices to record information in the diary.
watch a movie on the effects of good/bad peer influence.

topics.core_competency: The learner uses language related to wellbeing in the school environment.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: describe the school environment (k, u).
write a descriptive composition (k, u, s).
differentiate types of schools (k, u).
use adverbs (k, u, s).
appreciate school routines (v, a).
explain what news is (k, u).
identify various sources of news and how to extract it (k, u).
present news on different platforms (s).
fill in forms, identity cards and so on (s, gs).
understand the importance of school rules (k, u).
identify the types and causes of strikes in schools (k, u).

suggested_learning_activities.description: teacher probes learners to brainstorm on what environment is.
in their groups, learners list ten things found at school.
learners name five different categories of people found at school.
learners name different places at school.
the teacher tasks learners to draw a map of their school and locate different places on it.
teacher provides a sample descriptive text.
teacher guides learners to identify elements/principles/characteristics of a descriptive text from the sample.
learners write a composition of 150 words describing the school environment.
through question and answer, the teacher guides the learner to outline the types of schools that are common in Uganda.
in their groups learners analyse what differentiates the schools/ different curricula.
teacher probes leaners to explain what an adverb is.
leaners identify adverbs from a text provided by the teacher.
leaners construct sentences using given adverbs.
teacher probes leaners to narrate what happens in a normal school day.
in groups, learners discuss different programmes that take place in the school and their rationale.
the learners interpret school schedules/lists and tables, for example a timetable.
teacher guides leaners to draw a class routine chart.
learners are tasked to fill in important events on a class calendar.
teacher probes learners to explain what news is.
in their groups learners identify the different ways in which news is delivered in their community.
the learners mention/talk about their favourite news presenters on both radio/tv and the time of broadcast.
in their groups, learners discuss qualities/characteristics of a good news reader/format of a good news article.
learners listen to news on a radio broadcast.
learners read a news article extracted from one of the local dailies.
as project work the learners are tasked to gather news for the school newspaper/newsletter.
teacher groups learners and asks them to study sample forms and other official documents.
teacher guides learners to analyse and extract key information from the sample forms and other official documents.
in their groups, the learners fill in the forms and other official documents as guided by the teacher.
teacher probes learners to explain what “rules” are.
in groups teacher guides learners to reflect and discuss examples of rules in their family/community.
learners outline rules in their school in their groups.
teachers brainstorm with learners the importance of family/social rules.
in groups, learners discuss the importance of school rules.
learners present the outcomes of their discussion in a plenary.
teachers and learners brainstorm the meaning of strikes.
teacher guides learners to identify types of strikes. (sit-down, hunger strikes, demonstrations, laydown tools).
in groups, learners study a text/article on strikes and identify the causes.
in their groups, learners analyse the causes of strikes in schools.
learners discuss advantages and disadvantages of strikes at school in their groups.
learners suggest how strikes can be avoided.
in groups, learners prepare a persuasive speech to discourage others from striking.
learners deliver their speeches in a plenary.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: draws a sketch map of a school showing the locations of different places.
identifies adverbs from a given text.
writes a brief essay explaining why they like the news presenter they have selected.
presents news (relating to school and community) to the class/school assembly.
writes a persuasive speech discouraging others from striking.
debates on the impacts of strikes.
assumes the role of a school representative and gives a speech on the causes and impacts of school strikes.

project_requirements.project_scope_verbatim: as project work the learners are tasked to gather news for the school newspaper/newsletter.

suggested_uses: use a camera to take pictures of the school environment.
use the Internet to study about school strikes, and obtain images about objects and areas around the school to scupper class discussions.
use a computer to prepare a news item.

themes.theme_description: Focus on behaviour in public places and traditional naming ceremonies.

topics.core_competency: The learner understands appropriate behaviour and language used in public places.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: acquire appropriate vocabulary concerning public places such as shops, markets and hospitals (k, u).
explain activities pertaining to buying and selling (k, u, v, a, gs).
write a dialogue (s).
use tenses (k, u, s).
describe activities in hospitals (as public places) using appropriate vocabulary and punctuation (k, u).
develop customer care skills and marketing skills (gs).
recognise dress codes for different public places (v, a, gs).
describe an incident witnessed in a public place (k, u, s).

suggested_learning_activities.description: the teacher asks learners to study a map extract of a local trading centre or town.
teacher guides learners to interpret the map extract and guides them to identify specific public places.
leaners read a text provided by the teacher on public places.
in groups, learners identify specific words used in different public places.
learners construct sentences using the words they have identified (in 4 above).
learners make a visit to a nearby trading centre and interact with the community.
teacher guides learners to interpret public signs and notices.
learners roleplay a bargain for a commodity during a transaction in a market.
in groups, learners identify the appropriate negotiation and persuasion skills, phrases and sentences in marketing or buying a commodity.
teacher groups learners and tasks them to act a transaction.
learners study a sample dialogue in groups.
teacher guides learners to write a conversation of one page (8-10 pairs) on an activity between a buyer and seller carried out in a market/shop.
learners act a telephone conversation as the teacher observes.
learners respond to an exercise on a telephone conversation.
teacher provides learners with a sample text with varied tenses.
teacher guides the learners to identify all the different tenses in the text and their tense markers.
learners write sentences in different tenses. (present, past and future).
teacher groups learners and tasks them to identify, draw and name five objects found in hospital.
in groups, learners name five categories of people found in the hospital and their roles.
teacher pairs learners and tasks them to engage in a telephone conversation between a patient and doctor.
teacher guides learners as they demonstrate conversation etiquette.
teacher brainstorms with learners on what attracts them to buy certain items on the market.
in groups, learners share their personal experiences.
teacher provides a text containing different products for learners to choose an item/product and try to convince customer to buy it.
in pairs, learners role play/dramatise number (3) above.
learners write an advert to market an item/product as guided by the teacher.
learners make an exhibition of the products.
respond to news on a market survey and answer questions related to it.
listen to a radio advert on an item.
teacher guides learners to identify different professions that have specific dress codes.
learners brainstorm on the rationale for the dress codes.
learners describe how a person working in any one public building/location should dress.
teacher provides an oral or written account of a real or imaginary incident witnessed in a local centre, for instance, a fistfight, an accident or a theft for learners to study.
in plenary leaners vividly describe an incident, such as a fight, or an accident they witnessed.
learners produce well-structured pieces of writing of one page, which clearly express an argument or specific viewpoint using a wide range of language related to public places.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: identifies types of public places and describes activities carried out in them.
writes a composition of 100-150 words about an experience in any one public place.
role-plays the interaction between a buyer and seller in a marketplace.
writes a conversation between a doctor and patient of about one page.
listens and responds to a radio advert on a product and answers related questions (the advert can be recorded or read to the class).
writes a composition of 200 words giving a first or second-hand account of an incident.

suggested_uses: use a camera to take pictures of public places, local signposts and images to support classroom discussions.
use an online Geographical Information System (GIS) to obtain an insight in the plan, map interpretation and location.

topics.core_competency: The learner appreciates traditions and rituals of baptism and naming.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: explain how (ways in which) people acquire names (k, u, v, a).
use key vocabulary applicable to baptismal/ aqeeqah and naming activities. (u, k)
state the importance of rituals associated with baptismal/ aqeeqah and naming ceremonies. (u, v/a)
understand how nouns and verbs are formed.
identify the values of bearing a name that reflects ones’ origin. (u, v, a)
identify songs related to naming (k, u).

suggested_learning_activities.description: learners talk about the meanings of their names.
teacher brainstorms with learners on how and when children are named.
in groups, learners describe different ways in which children/people acquire names.
in their groups, learners explain situations that induce people to give names to their children.
teacher guides learners to list and categorise names according to situations of naming.
in their groups learners identify surnames with masculine and feminine equivalents. (e.g. Ngobi vs Nangobi- Lusoga, Oketcho vs Nyaketcho– Dhopadhola)
as project work, learners collect twenty surnames and investigate their meanings and origins.
learners study a text on baptism.
teacher guides learners to identify and discuss key vocabularies used in the text.
learners use vocabularies identified to construct sentences (god-father, god-mother, overcoming Satan, sprinkling water, candle, etc.)
teacher guides learners to describe a naming ceremony they ever attended.
learners identify the different rituals associated with naming.
in their groups, learners analyse the importance of the rituals identified above.
teacher guides leaners to identify five proverbs associated with naming.
learners recap the meanings of noun and verb with examples.
using appropriate examples, teacher demonstrates to learners how nouns and verbs are formed.
in groups, learners study a text on noun and verb formation and respond to questions on the text.
teacher gives a list of names from different ethnic groups, religions and clans and asks for learners’ opinion.
learners brainstorm on the values/importance of names.
teacher guides learners to point out at least two levels of identity associated with names.
teacher sings a song related to naming.
teacher asks learners to explain the subject and purpose of the song.
in groups learners identify other examples of naming songs and perform them.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: reads a text and responds to questions on baptism /aqeeqah and naming.
states five names of personal significance (e.g. names of members of his/her family) and describes the circumstances surrounding their meanings/ origins.
states a name that he/she would love to give to his/her child and gives reasons.
compiles a list of proverbs associated with names in his/her culture.
collects and writes various naming/ baptismal songs in his/her culture.
composes and performs a song related to naming.

project_requirements.project_scope_verbatim: as project work, learners collect twenty surnames and investigate their meanings and origins.

suggested_uses: listen or watch recordings of traditional naming ceremonies.

themes.theme_description: Focus on careers, professions, and job application skills.

topics.core_competency: The learner understands different occupations, professions and careers and their related terminologies.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: identify the the various professions in the world of work (k, u).
identify terminologies used in the different professions and occupations (k, u).
identify different places of work for the various professions /occupations (k, u).
appreciate the dress code for the different professions (v, a, gs).
write a CV (s, gs)
write an application letter (s, gs).
write an apology letter (s, gs)
describe what comedy is (k).
explain characteristics of comedy (k).
state the merits and demerits of comedy (k).
use personal pronouns (k, u).

suggested_learning_activities.description: teacher asks leaners to identify the various professions/careers in their communities and schools.
learners talk about their career interests and why.
teacher guides learners to identify other professions and occupations in the world of work.
individually learners write a one-page essay explaining their career interests.
learners mention titles of people working in different professions/occupations.
teacher guides learners to derive professions from verbs.
learners identify professionals and what they do e.g. teacher-teaches, a doctor-dragonises /prescribes /treats, a lawyer-defends/prosecutes suspects, driver-drives,etc.
teacher identifies terminologies and tasks learners to use them to construct sentences.
teacher guides learners mention the equipment and tools used in different occupations.
learners mention the work places of their relatives and friends.
teacher provides learners with a text on different professions and workplaces. (e.g. mechanic- garage, judge-court, shopkeeper – shop, teacher-school, doctor-hospital, etc.
learners answer questions on the text.
teacher provides leaners with a chart having samples of different dress codes and asks them to match them with corresponding professions.
in groups, learners describe dress codes of other professionals they know.
learners discuss reasons for the different dress codes in their groups.
teacher guides learners on how to present information about themselves.
learners talk about themselves - bringing out necessary information. (random selection).
teacher provides a sample cv for learners to study.
learners identify aspects of a cv basing on the sample (format).
individually learners write personal cvs.
learners study a sample application letter.
from the sample letter, teacher asks learners to identify parts of an application letter (format).
teacher provides a sample job advert to which he/she responds with learners.
in an exercise, learners write an application letter
teacher asks learners whether they have ever wronged any one.
then asks them to share how they respond when they have done something wrong.
a role-play in which a learner is apologising to a superior (e.g. a parent, teacher, prefect, priest, police officer etc.)
learners study a sample apology letter identifying key parts.
in an exercise learners write an apology.
teacher brainstorms with learners on what comedy is and who comedians are.
learners describe any comedian they know.
learners identify other persons they consider to be comedians in their community, school, media and beyond explaining why.
in groups teacher guides learners to suggest what makes a comedian comic.
learners brainstorm on why people perform comedy.

in their groups, learners discuss the benefit of comedy in society, e.g. entertainment, stress reliever, excitement, income generation, talent expo/development, mirror what happens in society, advocacy.
in a plenary, learners present their responses to (6) above.
teacher guides learners to recap their understanding of pronouns.
using examples, teacher illustrates to learners what personal pronouns are (singular and plural).
teacher guides learners on how to construct sentences using personal pronouns.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: answers comprehension questions about a given passage on professions/ occupations.
writes a composition explaining his/her profession/ occupation interest.
fills in a table on the different professions and their respective places of work.
translates texts on different professions.
debates on topics related to places of work e.g. “uniforms should be abolished at places of work.”
writes an application letter for a job attaching a c.v.
presents a comic skit on a topic/issue selected from the learners’ suggestions.
writes a composition about a comedy s/he enjoy and the lessons learnt.
writes a composition on the merits and demerits of comedy to society.
matches tools and equipment with their respective professions/ occupations in a matching exercise.
draws a table to show personal pronouns and their plural forms.
writes a report about a tour to a place of work highlighting activities taking place there.

suggested_uses: use a project to display to various dress codes for different professions.
use e-mail, social media, SMS or wikis to share information and collaborate with one another.
